newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Woqats aims at Europe Internet quotes, news market.
newsitem.headline: Woqats aims at Europe Internet quotes, news market.

text.p: Belgian start-up firm Woqats on Wednesday launched an Internet site providing investors with real-time stock quotes and financial news.
"We want to become the leading European website for real-time financial information," Woqats general manager Dimitri Verboomen, 27, told a news conference.
World Online Quote And Trading System (Woqats) has signed contracts with several stock exchanges, British money and securities broker Harlow Butler and news agency AFX to re-sell quotes and news.
Unlike similar U.S. firms such as Quote.Com, PC Quote and InterQuote, Woqats wants to focus on European markets and will make its services available in five European languages.
Verboomen said Woqats hopes to have 5,000 subscribers by the end of 1997.

Woqats is aiming its service at clients such as investment club members, sophisticated private investors, corporate management and professional investors who cannot afford the services offered by leading financial news agencies.
Woqats's services aim to turn an investor's personal computer into a trading-room terminal.
To do this, Woqats does not rely on a standard HTML link, but uses a Java application which continuously refreshes the data on its www.woqats.com website.
Woqats, with its existing staff of three, plans later to offer share trading facilities, via deals with brokerages in the countries in which it has customers.
The driving forces behind Woqats are two other Belgian companies; trading room services company Tradeware Technology and computer and telecoms services company Axime/Sligos/Marben group.
